correctness.rationale: The conditional two-stage thinning comparison uses convexity of Bernstein-polynomial binomial expectations at each fixed potential-contact count. Equal conditional means give convex ordering of contributions, sums preserve convex order, and a later independent branching stage preserves convex order through nonnegative-increment discrete convexity. Adjacent swaps yield the full sorting theorem. Independent variance recursion yields the exact factorial-second-moment swap gap. A PGF commutator plus strict positivity establishes the elimination boundary when offspring branching is possible. Directly executed standard-library exact Fraction verification passed 1,680 assertions; finite checks do not replace the universal proof. Assumptions are independent contact counts, strictly positive thinning, a finite horizon, and finite second moment; no cumulative-case result is claimed.

originality.rationale: The closest generational-PGF intervention article contains forecasting machinery but not the exact fixed-multiset all-permutation convex-order result. Two primary varying-environment Galton-Watson sources cover survival and limits rather than a finite-horizon thinning commutator. A related cumulative two-generation intervention calculation is not logically dominating because it treats a different observable with different means, and a deterministic-SIR total-incidence intervention study has a different process and objective. The analytic pair-swap inequality, variance identity and sharp branching boundary have no directly covering antecedent in inspected materials. This is a qualified self-review originality verdict; unsearched broader stochastic-order rearrangement results are a residual risk.
residual_risks: A general stochastic-order or rearrangement theorem beyond the three full-text primary comparators could imply the result without sharing the application vocabulary.
The exact priority of the convex-order ordering in any broader time-inhomogeneous branching literature has not been independently certified.
The distinction from cumulative-incidence intervention policy results is essential.

value.rationale: For the same multiset of intervention levels, every chronological arrangement gives identical expected new infections in a chosen terminal generation but potentially different elimination probability, variance, and every convex tail-loss metric. The universal sorting rule, factorial-moment sensitivity formula, strict nonbranching cutoff, and certified rational example provide meaningful benchmarks for how timing redistributes terminal-generation outbreak risk. This is not an exercise in computing a single example; it is a distributional comparison over every horizon and every finite-variance potential-contact law. The conclusion does not generalize to cumulative infections or susceptible-depleted epidemics without additional proof.
